visual_action: A montage of clips on an airport tarmac shows several men being escorted by officials from a white van to a large, white U.S. Coast Guard propeller plane. The officials' faces are blurred. The men, dressed in civilian clothes, are led one-by-one toward the aircraft. One shot is a close-up of a man's feet in ankle shackles as he boards. Other shots show the men being processed or searched by an official before walking towards the plane. The video includes close-up B-roll shots of the airplane's exterior, such as its tail and propeller.

cast.name: Unnamed deportees
cast.evidence: Multiple men are shown being escorted onto a plane for deportation, and the on-screen text describes them as 'illegal criminal aliens'.

cast.name: Unnamed officials
cast.evidence: Several individuals with their faces blurred are shown escorting the deportees from a van to the plane.

cast.name: U.S. Coast Guard
cast.evidence: The text 'U.S. COAST GUARD' is clearly visible on the side of the airplane being used for the transport.

on_screen_text.text: Dozens of illegal criminal aliens depart for deportation 👋

spoken_summary: The video has no spoken dialogue, only ambient sounds from the airport tarmac, including the whirring noise of the plane's propellers.
audio_music: The audio consists entirely of diegetic, ambient sound from the airport tarmac. The prominent sound is the loud, continuous whirring of the propeller plane's engines, which runs throughout the video, creating a documentary-style, realistic atmosphere.
editing_pacing: The video is a montage with multiple quick cuts showing different stages of the deportation process from various angles. It includes wide shots of the tarmac, medium shots of individuals being escorted, and close-ups on details like ankle shackles and the plane itself.
cultural_references: The caption "You don’t have to go home but you can’t stay hereee" is a reference to a lyric from the 1998 song "Closing Time" by the band Semisonic.
central_claim: The U.S. government is actively enforcing immigration laws by deporting undocumented immigrants who have committed crimes.
intended_effect: To reassure supporters of strict immigration enforcement that the administration is taking action, and to project an image of strength on border security and crime.
